source.section: PDF p.16 Line 22 - Marriage penalty credit and Marriage Penalty Credit Worksheet lines 1-14; PDF p.17 qualified income; Form ND-1 line 22; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 60,000.00 + wages (person 1) 60,000.00 = 120,000.00. Federal taxable income = 120,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 88,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 88,500.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 88,500.00. Subtractions lines 5-16: none; line 17 = 0.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 88,500.00 - 0.00 = 88,500.00. Line 19 = 88,500.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (88,500.00 - 80,975.00) = 1.95% x 7,525.00 = 146.7375, to the cent 146.74; the Tax Table row 88,500 to 88,550 gives 147; expected uses the bracket formula on the exact income. Lines 21-23 credits: Marriage Penalty Credit Worksheet (not in the projection, shown for the difference): line 1 88,500.00; line 3a 60,000.00, line 3b 60,000.00; line 4 60,000.00; line 5 15,750.00; line 6 44,250.00; line 7 Single schedule tax on line 6 = 0.00; line 8 44,250.00; line 9 Single schedule tax on line 8 = 0.00; line 10 joint schedule tax on line 1 = 146.7375; line 11 = 0.00; line 12 = 146.7375; line 13 312.00; line 14 credit = 146.7375, 146.74. The projection does not take it (not_modelled, warn_when always), so credits stay 0.00 and expected overstates the form's net tax by 146.74. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 146.74. Here the form's credit takes the whole tax: each spouse's own 44,250.00 is in the Single 0% band, so line 25 on the form would be 0.00 against 146.74 expected.
accepted_approximations: Tax below 100,000 is figured on the exact income; the booklet uses a 50-dollar Tax Table row rounded to whole dollars.
The marriage penalty credit is left out.
